title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex
technique: Certaindex (answer-stabilization certainty) drives early exit, dynamic token allocation and gang scheduling in Dynasor serving of reasoning programs (CoT, SC, MCTS, REBASE)

optimized_metrics.evidence: Dynasor employs certaindex to adaptively allocate token budgets to reduce ... the compute cost
the compute cost, and enables gang scheduling to increase request SLO attainment and throughput.
reclaiming wasted compute without sacrificing accuracy.
gang scheduling to increase request SLO attainment and throughput.

headline_claim.text: up to 50% compute savings and 3.3× higher throughput in real workloads with no accuracy drop

reported_metrics.where: Fig 8a,b (program rate / SLO scale vs deadline attainment)
App. F ablation (mean latency of programs)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: System performance is evaluated by P90 deadline attainment, the percentage of queries completed within their deadlines.
metric_definitions.notes: Per-program (query) deadline, not per-token; sustainable rate = highest arrival rate with >=90% attainment ('P90 deadline attainment').

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Deadlines are calculated as the product of the SLO scale, the difficulty factor, and a base deadline, accounting for the additional time required for more challenging problems.
metric_definitions.notes: Difficulty-aware: difficulty factor 1/2/3 for always-correct/variable/always-incorrect queries from >100 oracle trials; SLO scale swept (1.3-4.7x tighter).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We apply finish-time fairness (§D.3.1) as the fairness metric and use latency / number of tokens as a proxy.
metric_definitions.notes: Program latency normalised by generated tokens (like Autellix's program token latency).

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we achieve ... cumulative tokens generated at a specific step (Table 3) as the proxy
metric_definitions.notes: Compute cost proxied by tokens generated across all branches of a reasoning program; accuracy-matched.

slo_spec: Deadline per reasoning program = SLO scale x difficulty factor x base deadline; attainment target P90; rate (programs/s) and SLO scale swept.
load_regime: Poisson program arrivals (programs/s) online; offline batch for token savings
tradeoff_acknowledged: Throughput in tokens/s is unchanged ('equal average throughput ... memory bound'); gains come from fewer tokens per program. Early exit risks dropping accuracy; paper keeps accuracy fixed.
models: Llama3.1-8B-Instruct, DeepSeek-distilled Qwen2.5 models, Skywork-7B, Llama2-7B
workloads: MATH-500, AIME24, AMC23, GSM8K with CoT, Self-Consistency, MCTS, REBASE
extractor_notes: Headline '3.3x higher throughput' is sustainable program arrival rate at P90 deadline attainment (program level), NOT tokens/s; paper states token throughput is equal across systems. Compute savings = fewer tokens at same accuracy. Gang scheduling is the PROGRAM_JCT lever; deadlines are per-program with difficulty-dependent scaling.
load_class_quote: Request arrivals follow ... a Poisson process with varying rates. [App F.3 online serving with Poisson arrivals; batch/offline tokens-to-accuracy workloads in Table 1 ('For offline workloads, we measure tokens-to-accuracy')]
